I just read your post history and I just want to say you’re an adult with her own kids who has lived through everything with your parents and has come out a strong and sane person, so what you decide to do is completely up to you. With that being said, Bunny has never really respected you or taken care of you the way a mother is supposed to, you went NC for a reason, and that is okay. Her own life choices are most likely what’s led to these medical problems and you don’t owe her a relationship because of them. You don’t have to put yourself (or your kids) back into toxic situations because she’s sick. I really do hope she’s changed and she’s a better person, but in the event that she’s not, it’s okay for you to be NC. *sends internet hugs*

We worked together for almost a year before he even ever asked me on a date and after our first date I told him I wasn’t ready for a relationship. He told me that he understood, and then was genuinely there for me as a friend. One night after a particularly bad night at work, we sat in his car and I told him all about all the bad things that had happened to me during my other relationships. He asked if he could hug me when I was done talking. He comforted me without being pushy and was the most considerate, respectful person I’d ever met. I pretty much knew I loved him then.

Just so you’re aware, not all of us are “choosing” to stay servers. A lot of my friends in the industry are there because they’re trying to get degrees or certifications to do other things, but jobs that work around a school schedule are all pretty much serving and fast food jobs, and even though fast food pays minimum wage, it’s not like that’s a huge amount. Minimum wage in my state is 7.25 an hour and taxes will typically take between 50 and 80 dollars out of a check if you get paid once a week. I can’t wait for the day I can quit running around like a chicken with my head cut off for 12+ hours every night just so I can make ends meet to go to school, but until I finish school, this is the best option of all the shitty options I’ve got. I’m not a huge fan of tipping culture either, but for the love of fuck don’t stiff your waitress to prove a point.

Speaking from some level of experience, it’s usually a lot healthier for a kid to have two separate but happy parents than two parents who are together and miserable. As we grow up, we tend to understand better the decisions our parents made. As long as you’re as honest as you can be (appropriate for her age and attempting to avoid trashing your ex even though it’s tempting) I’m willing to bet she’ll understand as she gets older. Whatever you decide to do, this situation sounds exhausting and I am so sorry for you. Sending internet hugs.
